ghrp-5.summary: The "Momany peptide": a GH-releasing peptide bodybuilders consider for muscle and leanness, studied in laboratory and anti-doping papers.

quick.overview:
GHRP-5 is a synthetic peptide in the growth hormone-releasing peptide family, also called the Momany peptide. People in muscle-building circles look at it for more muscle and a leaner body.

It is classed as an agonist of the ghrelin/growth hormone secretagogue receptor, so the idea is more GH release, higher GH and IGF-1, then more muscle and less fat. The published literature consists of anti-doping chemistry and a few laboratory studies, including one reporting that it also releases prolactin. No human clinical studies were found.
quick.how: It is discussed as an injectable research peptide in the same family as GHRP-1, -2, -4 and -6, usually alongside training and diet goals for muscle and leanness. Because there are no human studies, there is no established routine or timeline for results.
quick.risks: No human safety data were found. It is on the World Anti-Doping Agency prohibited list, so it is off limits in competitive sport, and it is not an approved medicine. The laboratory prolactin finding is one more unknown.

angle.text: GHRP-5, the Momany peptide, is grouped with GHRP-1, -2, -4 and -6 as a GH-releasing peptide that bodybuilders consider for muscle and leanness. The chain people describe is GH release, higher GH and IGF-1, then more muscle and less fat; published work so far is laboratory and anti-doping literature.

livoletide.summary: An investigational unacylated-ghrelin peptide built to reduce hunger in Prader-Willi syndrome, discussed for appetite control and a leaner body.

quick.overview:
Livoletide is an experimental peptide designed to curb the extreme hunger of Prader-Willi syndrome. Fat-loss followers watch it as an appetite lever: less hunger, lower intake, a leaner body.

It mimics unacylated ghrelin, a form of the hunger hormone that does not activate the usual ghrelin receptor, and it was meant to replace a reported relative shortage of that form in people with PWS. Its main phase 2b/3 trial (ZEPHYR, 158 participants) is recorded as terminated, and no study has tested it for appearance-related fat loss.
quick.how: It has only been used in clinical trials for hyperphagia in Prader-Willi syndrome. There is no consumer routine, and no data exist on how long any change would take in people seeking cosmetic fat loss.
quick.risks: It is investigational and has never been approved. Safety information comes from nonclinical and juvenile toxicity work and trial records. It was developed for a rare medical condition, and its effects in people without that condition are unknown.

angle.text: Livoletide is an investigational appetite peptide that acts like unacylated ghrelin to turn down hunger, which in theory means lower intake and a leaner body. It was built for hunger in Prader-Willi syndrome, and its pivotal trial was terminated.

lenomorelin-ghrelin.summary: Ghrelin, the stomach hunger hormone that also stimulates growth hormone, discussed as a lever on appetite and body composition.

quick.overview:
Ghrelin (INN lenomorelin) is the stomach hormone that signals hunger and prompts growth hormone release. Fat-loss and muscle communities discuss it because appetite and GH both shape body fat and muscle.

Once an octanoyl group is attached by the enzyme GOAT, ghrelin activates the GHS-R1a receptor in the brain, pituitary and gut, driving hunger and GH release. Administered ghrelin has been studied clinically in settings such as cancer cachexia and frailty. No study has tested it for appearance goals.
quick.how: Outside clinical research it appears mainly in discussions of appetite and GH rather than as a routine anyone follows. Its main clinical use has been to stimulate appetite and weight in wasting conditions.
quick.risks: Clinical use has been investigational. The sources reviewed give no safety summary, and it is not an approved appearance treatment. Because it raises hunger, effects on appetite run opposite to fat-loss goals.

angle.text: Ghrelin is the stomach hormone that raises hunger and stimulates growth hormone, so fat-loss and muscle communities discuss it as a lever on appetite and body composition. It has been studied in cachexia and frailty, not for cosmetic use.

cortistatin-14.summary: A somatostatin-related brain peptide that also binds ghrelin-type receptors, occasionally discussed for recovery and the GH axis.

quick.overview:
Cortistatin-14 is a short neuropeptide closely related to somatostatin, first noted for its activity in the cortex. Occasional recovery and GH-axis speculation comes from the fact that it also binds ghrelin-type receptors.

It shares 11 of 14 amino acids with somatostatin-14, binds all five somatostatin receptors, has been reported to bind GHS receptors in human pituitary tissue, and activates the itch receptor MRGPRX2. The literature is basic neuroscience, receptor pharmacology and a few small human endocrine studies. No trial has tested it for appearance, muscle or recovery.
quick.how: It is a research peptide with no approved product, so there is no established routine. It appears in discussion mainly as a curiosity in the GH and recovery space.
quick.risks: Human safety data are essentially limited to small endocrine studies. It has no approved product or regulatory status as a medicine, and its itch-receptor activity is one documented effect.

angle.text: Cortistatin-14 is a brain neuropeptide related to somatostatin that also binds ghrelin-type receptors, which draws occasional speculation about recovery and the GH axis. Published work is basic science and receptor pharmacology.

lum-201.summary: LUM-201 (ibutamoren) is an oral GH secretagogue that physique users discuss as a pill route to higher GH and IGF-1 for muscle and leanness.

quick.overview:
LUM-201 is the development name for ibutamoren (MK-0677), a daily oral drug that stimulates the body's own growth hormone release. Physique users discuss it as a pill-form route to higher GH and IGF-1, aiming for more muscle and less fat.

It activates the GH secretagogue (ghrelin-type) receptor, prompting pulsatile GH release and raising IGF-1. It is being developed as an alternative to injections in children with growth hormone deficiency; Phase 2 trials reported growth responses in some children and a Phase 3 trial is under way. No study has examined it for appearance in healthy people.
quick.how: In trials it is a daily oral drug for children with diagnosed GH deficiency, with a pretreatment test proposed to identify who is likely to respond. In physique circles it is discussed as a pill alternative to GH injections.
quick.risks: It is investigational and not approved by any regulator. Safety data come from pediatric trials, with long-term safety extensions registered. Data in healthy adults seeking looks outcomes are not available.

angle.text: LUM-201 is ibutamoren (MK-0677), an oral GH secretagogue that physique users discuss as a pill-form route to higher GH and IGF-1, meaning more muscle and less fat. Trials so far are in children with GH deficiency.

igf-1-des.summary: A truncated IGF-1 analogue forum users inject locally hoping to grow the jaw, chin and muscle; research is in cells and animals.

quick.overview:
IGF-1 DES (des(1-3)IGF-1) is a shortened form of IGF-1. Forum users discuss injecting it into the chin, jaw or neck, hoping to grow muscle and reshape the lower face.

Lacking three amino acids, it binds less to IGF binding proteins, and in lab assays it was more potent than full-length IGF-1 at stimulating protein synthesis in rat muscle cells. That local IGF-1 signalling is the chain proponents cite for tissue growth. The supporting work is in cell cultures and animals; no human study has tested it for muscle or facial appearance.
quick.how: Users describe local use in the target area, often stacked with other agents for facial remodelling. Reports are anecdotal, with no established timeline or results.
quick.risks: No human safety data exist and it has no approved human use. Animal work reported prostate overgrowth with IGF-1(des) expression, and elevated IGF signalling is described as a cancer-risk factor.

angle.text: Forum users inject IGF-1 DES locally hoping to grow the jaw, chin and neck, since local IGF-1 signalling drives tissue growth in lab assays. The evidence is cell and animal data on protein synthesis.

somatrogon.summary: A weekly prescription growth hormone for children with diagnosed GH deficiency, which raises growth velocity and comes up in height discussions.

quick.overview:
Somatrogon (Ngenla) is a once-weekly growth hormone injection approved in the US for children aged 3 and older whose bodies do not make enough growth hormone. It comes up in height discussions because GH drives growth velocity and, over time, final height.

It binds the growth hormone receptor, activates STAT5b signalling and raises IGF-1, promoting linear growth. Phase 3 trials compared it with daily somatropin in children with a diagnosed deficiency, and reviews describe non-inferior height velocity and similar safety to daily GH. No study has tested it for height in children without a deficiency.
quick.how: It is prescribed by specialists as a weekly injection in place of daily GH for diagnosed growth failure, with growth tracked over months and years of treatment.
quick.risks: The label lists warnings such as neoplasm risk, glucose intolerance, intracranial hypertension, fluid retention, hypoadrenalism, hypothyroidism and hypersensitivity. It is prescription-only and approved for diagnosed deficiency.

angle.text: Somatrogon is a weekly prescription growth hormone that raises growth velocity in children with diagnosed GH deficiency, which is why height-focused people follow it. Trials are in children with deficiency.

lonapegsomatropin.summary: A weekly prescription growth hormone prodrug for children and adults with diagnosed GH deficiency, mentioned in height-focused circles.

quick.overview:
Lonapegsomatropin (Skytrofa) is a once-weekly growth hormone injection approved by the FDA in 2021 for children and adults with growth hormone deficiency. It is mentioned in height-focused circles because GH drives growth velocity.

It is a pegylated prodrug that releases somatropin, which binds the GH receptor and acts partly through IGF-1. Phase 3 trials compared it with daily somatropin in treatment-naive and switched children. All trials involve people with a diagnosed deficiency; none tests it for height in people without one.
quick.how: It is prescribed as a weekly injection for children aged 1 and older weighing at least 11.5 kg, and for adults with GH deficiency, replacing daily GH.
quick.risks: The label lists warnings including neoplasm risk, glucose intolerance, intracranial hypertension, fluid retention, hypoadrenalism, hypothyroidism and hypersensitivity. It is prescription-only.

angle.text: Lonapegsomatropin is a weekly prescription GH prodrug that raises growth in children and adults with diagnosed deficiency, so it appears in height-focused circles. Its trials involve people with GH deficiency.

somapacitan.summary: A weekly albumin-binding growth hormone for diagnosed GH deficiency and some short-stature conditions, watched by height-focused users.

quick.overview:
Somapacitan (Sogroya) is a once-weekly growth hormone injection. In the US it is labelled for GH deficiency in children and adults, and for several pediatric short-stature conditions, so height-focused users watch it.

It is a GH derivative that binds albumin reversibly, extending its action, and binds the GH receptor with effects partly mediated by IGF-1. Phase 3 trials covered adults (REAL 1) and children (REAL 4), and reviews describe non-inferior height velocity and similar safety to daily growth hormone. No study has tested it for height in people without a diagnosis.
quick.how: It is prescribed as a weekly injection in diagnosed conditions: pediatric GH deficiency, born small for gestational age, Noonan syndrome growth failure, idiopathic short stature, and adult GH deficiency.
quick.risks: The label lists warnings including neoplasm risk, glucose intolerance, intracranial hypertension, fluid retention, hypoadrenalism, hypothyroidism and hypersensitivity. It is prescription-only.

angle.text: Somapacitan is a weekly prescription growth hormone that raises growth velocity in diagnosed GH deficiency and some short-stature conditions, which is why height-focused users watch it. Studies cover those diagnosed groups.

mecasermin.summary: Prescription recombinant IGF-1 for children with rare severe IGF-1 deficiency, raised in height forums as a growth lever.

quick.overview:
Mecasermin (Increlex) is lab-made IGF-1 given by injection, approved in the US for children 2 and older with severe primary IGF-1 deficiency, or GH gene deletion with antibodies to GH. It is raised in height forums because IGF-1 mediates growth.

It replaces the IGF-1 that GH would normally trigger, acting on the type 1 IGF receptor to stimulate growth at the growth plates, and also lowers blood glucose in an insulin-like way. Published trials and registries involve children with this rare, defined deficiency, not people with normal IGF-1.
quick.how: It is prescribed by specialists as an injection for children with the defined deficiency, taken with meals because of its glucose-lowering effect, with growth tracked over time. The label states it is not a substitute for GH in GH's approved uses.
quick.risks: The label lists hypoglycemia (including seizures), allergic reactions, intracranial hypertension, enlarged tonsils, slipped capital femoral epiphysis, scoliosis progression and malignancy. It is prescription-only and not indicated after growth plates close.

angle.text: Mecasermin is prescription recombinant IGF-1 that stimulates the growth plates in children with severe primary IGF-1 deficiency, so it comes up in height forums. It has been studied in that narrow group.

pegvisomant.summary: Prescription GH-receptor blocker for acromegaly; it lowers IGF-1 and serves as a reference point for GH-driven facial and bone change.

quick.overview:
Pegvisomant (Somavert) is an injectable drug that blocks the growth hormone receptor. It is approved for acromegaly, where excess GH enlarges the jaw, brow, hands and feet, so it appears in appearance discussions as the opposite of a GH booster.

It binds the GH receptor and prevents GH from signalling, which lowers IGF-1, the goal being to normalize IGF-1 in people who responded inadequately to surgery or radiation. Its cosmetic relevance is as a reference point for how much GH shapes facial and bone growth; no published study tests it for cosmetic use.
quick.how: It is used under specialist care as an injected treatment for acromegaly, with IGF-1 levels monitored to guide treatment.
quick.risks: The label lists liver enzyme elevations and liver toxicity, hypoglycemia in patients with diabetes, injection-site lipohypertrophy and hypersensitivity. It is prescription-only.

angle.text: Pegvisomant blocks the GH receptor and lowers IGF-1, the opposite of a GH booster, and is used in acromegaly where excess GH enlarges the jaw, brow and hands. In appearance circles it serves as a reference for GH-driven facial change.

bivamelagon.summary: Investigational oral MC4R agonist that targets the brain's appetite pathway, tested for hypothalamic obesity.

quick.overview:
Bivamelagon is an experimental once-daily oral drug that activates the MC4R, a brain receptor involved in appetite and weight regulation. Fat-loss followers watch it as a possible appetite-control route to a leaner look.

It stimulates MC4R signalling in the brain's weight-regulating pathway, the chain being lower hunger, lower intake and less body fat. A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2 trial in acquired hypothalamic obesity (weight gain after hypothalamic damage) was reported in the Journal of the Endocrine Society in 2025, with a long-term extension study starting afterward. No data exist in cosmetic or general fat-loss use.
quick.how: It has been used only in clinical trials, as a once-daily pill in people with hypothalamic obesity. There is no consumer routine.
quick.risks: Not approved anywhere. Safety data are limited to early trials in a small patient group, so effects in other people are unknown.

angle.text: Bivamelagon is an oral MC4R agonist that acts on the brain's appetite pathway, so hunger and intake fall and body fat follows. It has been studied in phase 2 for weight gain after hypothalamic damage.

rm-718.summary: Experimental weekly MC4R agonist aimed at the brain's appetite pathway, in early trials for rare obesity syndromes.

quick.overview:
RM-718 is an experimental weekly-dosed drug that activates the MC4R pathway of appetite regulation. Fat-loss followers watch it as a possible route to appetite control and a leaner physique.

As an MC4R agonist, it targets the pathway that lowers hunger signalling, the chain being reduced appetite, lower intake, then lower body weight and fat. A phase 1/2 study of 111 participants, including healthy volunteers and people with hypothalamic obesity or Prader-Willi syndrome, began in March 2024. No results or cosmetic data have been published.
quick.how: It is used only within the clinical study, designed for weekly dosing. No consumer routine exists.
quick.risks: Not approved, and no published safety results were located. The only available source is the trial registration.

angle.text: RM-718 is a weekly MC4R agonist that acts on the brain's appetite pathway, so hunger signalling drops and body weight and fat follow. It is in early trials for rare obesity syndromes.

pl-8177.summary: Experimental oral MC1r peptide linked to melanocortin pigment signalling, studied in ulcerative colitis rather than tanning.

quick.overview:
PL-8177 is an experimental oral peptide that activates the melanocortin 1 receptor, the receptor family linked to skin pigmentation. Tanning-peptide readers connect it to melanin signalling and a deeper tan.

It mimics alpha-MSH at MC1r. Its studied purpose is inflammation: preclinical work with PL-8177 and PL-8331 looked at preventing and reversing intestinal and ocular inflammation in animal models, and a phase 2a trial in active ulcerative colitis (n=16) began in September 2022. No studies were found of it for skin pigmentation or appearance.
quick.how: It has been used as an oral peptide in clinical research for ulcerative colitis. No tanning routine or timeline exists.
quick.risks: Not approved. Human safety data are limited to early-phase trials.

angle.text: PL-8177 is an MC1r agonist that tanning-peptide readers connect to melanocortin-driven melanin signalling and a deeper tan. It has been studied in inflammatory bowel and eye models.

shu-9119.summary: A lab melanocortin antagonist used in rodent appetite research as a reference tool for how melanocortin signalling shapes body weight.

quick.overview:
SHU-9119 is a research peptide that blocks melanocortin receptors. It enters fat-loss discussions as the tool scientists use to switch off appetite-regulating signalling, which clarifies how melanocortin agonists work.

It antagonizes MC3R and MC4R in the brain, opposing the signal of alpha-MSH. In rats, it was infused into the brain's third ventricle to study appetite, body weight and insulin action, and blocking this pathway increased feeding. No human studies were found.
quick.how: It is used only in laboratory animal research. There is no human routine.
quick.risks: No human safety data exist and it has no approved use. In animals, blocking this pathway increased feeding and altered insulin action, the opposite of a fat-loss effect.

angle.text: SHU-9119 is a melanocortin antagonist used in rodent studies to block appetite-regulating signalling, which is how it enters fat-loss discussions. Its appearance relevance is as a research reference for melanocortin agonists.

s-23.summary: A potent nonsteroidal SARM sold as a gray-market research chemical, taken for muscle gain; it was developed as a male contraceptive candidate.

quick.overview:
S-23 is a selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) developed by GTx, Inc. as a possible male hormonal contraceptive. Users take it hoping for muscle gain and a fuller physique with fewer steroid-like effects.

It is a nonsteroidal compound that binds the androgen receptor more tightly than the older SARM andarine (reported Ki of about 1.7 nM), and animal studies describe a favourable ratio of anabolic to androgenic effects. In animals it suppressed sperm production dose-dependently, with recovery after treatment stopped. No human trials are described in the sources consulted.
quick.how: It is sold online as a research chemical and used in physique circles, usually alongside training and diet. Reports are anecdotal, with no established timeline.
quick.risks: No human safety data are described. SARMs as a class are banned by WADA, and compounds sold online as research chemicals have been reported to be mislabeled. Class-level reports include liver enzyme elevation and suppression of the body's own testosterone production. It was reported as a designer drug by 2020.

angle.text: S-23 is a SARM users take hoping for muscle gain by binding the androgen receptor, building a more muscular physique with fewer steroid-like effects. Muscle effects come from animal work.

s-40503.summary: A nonsteroidal SARM with tissue-selective androgen receptor activity, described in rat osteoporosis models and detectable in doping tests.

quick.overview:
S-40503 is an experimental nonsteroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) noted in muscle-building circles for its tissue-selective activity, which is linked to lean mass.

It binds the androgen receptor with nanomolar affinity and preferentially over other nuclear receptors. It was described in 2003 in rat osteoporosis models, where it showed bone-building activity; in orchiectomized rats given it for 4 weeks, researchers compared its bone effects with dihydrotestosterone. Later literature comes mostly from anti-doping research. No human clinical trials are described.
quick.how: It is known mostly from the research and doping-control literature; no established routine or timeline for appearance goals exists.
quick.risks: No human safety data are described. SARMs are prohibited by WADA, and doping-control laboratories have developed methods to detect S-40503 in human plasma.

angle.text: S-40503 is a SARM noted in muscle-building circles for tissue-selective androgen receptor activity, linked to lean mass and firmer physique. It was studied in rat osteoporosis models, where it showed bone-building activity.

lgd-2226.summary: An experimental quinolinone SARM studied in animals for muscle and bone effects, sold as a research chemical for muscle gain.

quick.overview:
LGD-2226 is an oral, nonsteroidal SARM reported in 2006. Users take it hoping to add muscle and a more muscular physique with less prostate stimulation than testosterone.

It binds and activates the androgen receptor. In animals it showed anabolic effects on muscle and bone, with comparatively smaller effects on prostate weight and luteinizing hormone than testosterone. It was researched for muscle wasting and osteoporosis, not cosmetic use. No published human trial was identified.
quick.how: It is sold online as a research chemical in physique-focused circles, typically alongside training and diet. Reports are anecdotal.
quick.risks: No human safety data exist. SARMs as a class have been linked to liver enzyme elevations and hormone suppression, are banned in sport, and are unapproved by the FDA.

angle.text: LGD-2226 is a SARM that users take hoping to add muscle by activating the androgen receptor, with less prostate stimulation than testosterone. Animal studies showed anabolic effects on muscle and bone.

lgd-2941.summary: A quinolinone SARM that muscle-building communities treat as a lean mass candidate; its development was discontinued after Phase I.

quick.overview:
LGD-2941 (also LGD-122941) is a nonsteroidal SARM of the quinolinone class, explored for muscle wasting, low testosterone and bone loss. Muscle-building communities treat it as a lean mass candidate.

Like other SARMs, it is designed to activate the androgen receptor selectively in muscle and bone, the chain being anabolic signalling in muscle and more lean mass. Its development has reportedly stopped after a Phase I trial was discontinued. Very little is published beyond its chemistry, and no human results were identified.
quick.how: There is little community material and no established routine for appearance use.
quick.risks: No safety data are public. It is unapproved, and SARMs generally are banned in sport.

angle.text: LGD-2941 is a quinolinone SARM that muscle-building communities treat as a lean mass candidate, designed to activate the androgen receptor selectively in muscle. It was investigated for cachexia and hypogonadism, then discontinued after Phase I.

lgd-3303.summary: An oral nonsteroidal SARM from Ligand Pharmaceuticals discussed for muscle gain; studied in rats and horses.

quick.overview:
LGD-3303 is an experimental oral SARM from Ligand Pharmaceuticals, discussed by people seeking muscle gain through selective androgen receptor activity.

It activates the androgen receptor; in rats it stimulated muscle strongly while only partially stimulating prostate tissue. Published work covers animal and in vitro studies of its pharmacokinetics, muscle and bone effects and effects on sexual behaviour in female rats, plus metabolite detection studies in horses. No registered human trial was found.
quick.how: It is known mostly from preclinical literature; no established routine or timeline exists for people.
quick.risks: There are no human safety data. SARMs as a class are unapproved, banned in sport, and linked in reports to liver injury.

angle.text: LGD-3303 is an oral SARM discussed by people seeking muscle gain through selective androgen receptor activity, which in rats stimulated muscle strongly while only partly stimulating prostate. Published work covers animal and in vitro studies.
